turns.user: I validated an ordinary single ticket and transfer from metro M2 to M3, staying in the metro network and continuing forward.
turns.agent:
That transfer is allowed under the snapshot guidance: an ordinary single ticket permits a change between metro lines when you continue in the same direction. Since you validated the ticket and stayed within the metro network, the M2-to-M3 change you describe fits that rule; you don’t need a second ordinary single just for that metro transfer.

This is based on the 5 November 2026 snapshot, not live verification. See BKK’s Single ticket page for current official rules.

turns.user: Now I want to take M3 back in the opposite direction. Can I keep using that ticket?
turns.agent:
No—use a new ordinary single ticket for the trip back in the opposite direction. The metro-line transfer allowance is for continuing in the same direction; it doesn’t turn one single ticket into a return ticket. The ticket you used for the M2-to-M3 journey won’t cover reversing direction on M3.

That follows the 5 November 2026 snapshot; see BKK’s Single ticket page for current rules.
